errors.text: The proposed material is a generic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni or refractory alloy rather than AuCoCuNiPt, so it cannot reproduce the element-specific Au/Cu surface segregation and evaporation mechanism.

The hypothesis treats configurational entropy, lattice distortion, and sluggish diffusion as the primary stabilizers, whereas the target finding is active, non-sluggish diffusion and kinetically controlled instability.
The long-duration 600–1000 °C argon anneal is fundamentally different from the 298–973 K, 1 K/s in situ vacuum-heating protocol and may introduce unrelated coarsening or equilibration mechanisms.

The predicted failure modes emphasize grain growth, Ostwald ripening, intermetallic formation, or amorphization rather than Au/Cu shell formation, melting, evaporation, particle loss, and shape evolution.
